title: Review of c07's wall-tilt negative: replicated on seed 3 (no cell moves more than 1.9 body lengths at a_s = 0, 3, 7; a_s=7 dies out)
summary: Fresh seed 3, labkit runs of world.py with WORLD_P a_s = 0, 3, 7 (T=10000, spf 100). Max body lengths 1.5 / 1.9 / 1.6, max speed <= 0.012. a_s=0: 17 walled cells, 11 persistent splits (gen 3). a_s=3: the tilt thins the population (11 cells at the end) and the sheet shows hollowed, fading cells and crescents that do not translate. a_s=7: all cells dead by t=10000 (c07's seed 1 kept a 5-cell drifting cluster). The negative result holds: the label-free wall-tilt drive does not make these ring cells swim, and stronger tilt kills them.

observations.I: rerun_a0/seed3/sheet.png and rerun_a3/seed3/sheet.png t=900-10000: discrete walled cells (17 and 11 at the end), max 1.5 and 1.9 body lengths (FACTS.md motion lines)

seeds_run.result: pass: no motility at any a_s; a_s=7 extinct (finding: 5 cells on seed 1)

verdicts.limitation: One fresh seed and three of the five a_s values; I did not vary sig_s or the wall-average width. The outcome at a_s=7 is seed-dependent (extinction here, a small drifting cluster on seed 1).
